name: Strawberry Pink
lede: Strawberry Pink is a deep yellowish pink dated by Maerz and Paul to 1912, and one of the rarest colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A single-source name
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary is the only source our library has for Strawberry Pink, dating it to 1912 and placing it on plate 1, swatch H10 [1]. It does not appear in Ridgway's 1912 standard, the 1955 ISCC-NBS lists, or the xkcd survey, so treat the name as resting on one dictionary's word [1]. The nearest named color on file is [[light-jasper-red]], 2.8 ΔE off [1]. Our own tagging files it among the Reds, alongside [[salmon]], [[coral]] and [[pink]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Strawberry Pink in only 19 of 23,781 paintings, about one in 1,250, as photographed, too rare for a reliable painter or company list [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1236 set of Tibetan lineage portraits, nearly seven centuries before Maerz and Paul's date, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name or a matching pigment existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.first_recorded: Maerz and Paul, 1930 (first recorded 1912, plate 1 H10)
